title: Monster Party
subtitle: Human Entertainment · Nintendo Entertainment System

body: Monster Party is Human Entertainment's NES platformer about Mark, a boy recruited by a winged creature named Bert to fight monsters in another world. His baseball bat provides the first weapon, while their magical connection allows him to transform temporarily into Bert. Bandai released the game in North America in 1989. The adventure combines recognisable horror creatures with deliberately ridiculous opponents, making the next doorway a source of uncertainty. A scene can resemble a familiar monster story before revealing that its menace is something much stranger.

As Mark, the player uses the bat to strike enemies and return certain projectiles. Transforming into Bert gives access to flight and another form of attack for a limited time. The change affects how an obstacle can be approached, with a stretch of ground that troubles the boy offering a different problem to his winged companion. Boss rooms supply short encounters and unexpected jokes. The game repeatedly changes the creature behind the door while keeping the player's small collection of actions recognisable.

Mummies, spiders and other traditional threats appear beside walking trousers, a talking caterpillar and even attacking food. Some references draw on Japanese folklore, creating a collection broader than a single film parody. A Japanese version was developed but never commercially released, and its prototype later became available. The released game preserves its peculiar mixture of cheerful cartoon character and unsettling surroundings. Its most memorable moments often come from refusing the expected monster, replacing a familiar danger with something that is funny precisely because it is so inappropriate.
story_headings: A baseball player enters a horror show
Two bodies for the same journey
Horror taken in an absurd direction
